https://www.baltictimes.com/_seb_banka__.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive 'SEB banka' Expands Its Office at SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS, One of Riga’s Most Modern Class A Office Complexes 2026-08-04 “SEB banka” is expanding its office at SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS, strengthening its presence in the Riga Central Business District and demonstrating its confidence in one of Latvia’s most modern Class A office developments. In July this year, the fit-out of nearly 550 m² of additional office space for “SEB banka” was completed in Building B of the complex, further reinforcing the bank’s status as the anchor tenant. The decision to increase its leased area reflects “SEB banka’s” long-term development plans, its high appreciation of the working environment and quality offered by SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS, and its deliberate strategy to invest in sustainable, modern office premises designed to meet future needs. “An increasing number of companies recognise the strategic advantages that the Riga Central Business District offers for business development. “SEB banka’s” decision to expand its office space at SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS almost simultaneously with the commissioning of the main part of the office complex is strong confirmation that companies increasingly value high-quality, sustainable workplaces designed to meet future needs. The decision to increase the leased area also strengthens “SEB banka’s” presence in the Riga Central Business District, which is developing into an important centre for business and finance. It demonstrates that companies regard an office not merely as a workplace, but as a strategic investment in business growth, employee experience and competitiveness,” says Evija Majevska, Commercial Director at “Linstow Baltic”. “Even before relocating last summer, we realised that we would like to expand our new office premises. We are therefore pleased that the architects had already anticipated this possibility and that the expansion could be implemented. The number of employees at our bank has grown in recent years, and we also wanted to fully accommodate the diverse needs of our colleagues. The expanded office area includes workstations, focus rooms for individual work, a spacious meeting and training room, a filming studio, and a parent room for occasions when colleagues visit us with very young children,” says Ieva Tetere, Chief Executive Officer of SEB banka. Spanning 12,000 m², SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS is a premium Class A office complex in the Riga Central Business District, opened in 2025. The building incorporates energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable technologies that reduce resource consumption and enhance tenant well-being. The development has received the BREEAM Outstanding sustainability certification with the highest rating in the Baltic states and has been recognised as one of Latvia’s most significant new office developments. The anchor tenant of the Class A office complex is “SEB banka”, while an additional 2,200 m² of leasable space remains available, offering flexible office and commercial premises ranging from 120 to 400 m² per floor. This gives companies of various sizes the opportunity to operate in central Riga in an environmentally friendly, technologically advanced workplace that supports employee well-being. Thanks to its strategic location next to Riga’s main multimodal public transport hub and the future “Rail Baltica” central station, SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS offers excellent accessibility at both local and international levels. The complex is located in the block bordered by Elizabetes, Ernesta Birznieka-Upīša, Dzirnavu and Satekles streets, integrating seamlessly into the dynamic environment of Riga Central Railway Station, the “Origo One” business centre and the “Origo” shopping centre. About “SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS” Opened in 2025, “SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS” is a sustainable Class A office complex in the “Riga Central Business District”, with a total area of 12,000 m². Located between Elizabetes, Ernesta Birznieka-Upīša, Dzirnavu and Satekles streets, and in close proximity to “Riga Central Railway Station” and the future “Rail Baltica” multimodal transport hub, the complex offers exceptional connectivity at a prime urban location. The complex combines the highest quality standards and excellent sustainability solutions, creating a modern and pleasant working environment for both employees and visitors, as evidenced by the received “BREEAM” certification for the final phase, with the highest rating in Latvia and the Baltics to date – “Outstanding”. Developed and managed by SIA “Linstow Baltic”, the anchor tenant is “SEB Bank”. More information: www.sateklesbiznesacentrs.lv About “Riga Central Business District” The “Riga Central Business District” is a strategically important, dynamic and multifunctional area in the heart of the city. Centred around the Riga Central Railway Station, it is emerging as the leading multimodal transport hub in the Baltics, driven by the development of the “Rail Baltica” infrastructure. The district is home to key commercial assets, including Class A office centers “SATEKLES BIZNESA CENTRS” and “Origo One”, the “Origo” shopping center, hotels, and other urban infrastructure. In line with “Linstow Baltic’s” development vision, the area is being purposefully transformed into a modern, multifunctional and integrated business environment that combines mobility, functionality, abundance of various amenities and services, sustainability and high-quality urban space. Photograph: FreeJaggiNow campaign/PA India British Sikh activist released from Delhi jail after nine-year detention Indian government issued with warning it would be in contempt of court if it failed to release Jagtar Singh Johal Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor Thu 1 Oct 2026 09.10 EDT First published on Thu 1 Oct 2026 08.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been released from a Delhi prison after the Indian high court warned the government it would be found in contempt of court if it continued to attempt to keep him in jail despite an 18 September court order releasing him on bail. Johal has been incarcerated for nine years without any full trial. The court order was issued after Johal’s lawyers issued a writ of habeas corpus alleging he was being detained against the express direction of the court. Johal’s nine-year detention on alleged terrorist offences, has been a cause of diplomatic tension between the UK and India, but campaigners have claimed the British government has not been active enough to secure his release or, alternatively, a full trial. The campaign group Reprieve says his case has never come to full trial largely because of the inability of the Indian government to assemble credible witnesses to back their claim that Johal transported £3,000 to France to fund a multinational extremist plot involving targeted killings in the Punjab in 2016-17. On Thursday morning, the high court in Delhi instructed the Indian government to release Johal by 2.30pm Indian time, giving government officials three hours to comply or find themselves risking contempt proceedings. In the end, he was released in the late afternoon wearing a red T-shirt to be greeted by friends, family and flowers. Documents shown to the court by Johal’s lawyers on behalf of his father-in-law as petitioner revealed that messages from the prison to the Ministry of Home Affairs seeking permission for his release had been left unanswered. His lawyers in their petition stated he had met all the bail conditions yet “the detainee has nevertheless not been released, and is being held in custody without the authority of any court, pending a ‘clarification’ sought by the jail from the Ministry of Home Affairs”. The petition added that no clarification from the ministry had been forthcoming, explaining: “Every day of such detention is a continuing violation of the detainee’s fundamental rights under article 21 of the constitution of India.” Johal has been detained by Indian authorities since 4 November 2017. He is facing eight charges of terrorism in the federal court, but had been cleared of largely similar charges by a Punjab court. He claims any initial confessions he gave were extracted under torture. The bail terms last week imposed 11 conditions, including surrender of passport, a personal bond of 500,000 Indian rupees (£3,930) with two sureties, fortnightly reporting to the investigating officer, prior intimation of any change of residence and a ban on travelling to the Punjab. He was also restricted from talking to media about the case directly or indirectly. The Indian government has alleged the Khalistan Liberation Force undertook the killings and Johal had “complete knowledge of the conspiracy” and was a KLF member. His Dumbarton-based brother Gurpreet Singh Johal said: “There have been so many setbacks and disappointments in the last nine years that I didn’t dare to believe it until I saw Jagtar walking out of the prison gates with my own eyes. The last two weeks have been torture – knowing that Jagtar had been granted bail, but the authorities were refusing to let him out. I’ll sleep well tonight, knowing that he’s not behind bars. “Tomorrow morning, the fight continues, because he’s still on trial and facing the death penalty for something he didn’t do, trapped in a sham legal process designed to punish him for standing up for human rights”. Reprieve’s deputy executive director, Dan Dolan, said: “While tonight is the first night in almost nine years that Jagtar Singh Johal is not caged in a prison cell, he still has the threat of a death sentence hanging over him. It should also be noted that, despite bail being ordered, the prison refused to release Jagtar until his family brought a habeas corpus petition and a judge warned the jail they’d be found in contempt of court”. The UK Foreign Office is understood to have been supporting recent calls for his release on bail after last week’s court order, as have two campaign groups in the UK Redress and Reprieve.
